title: Consolidated solution: orchestration by scripts, a smaller plugin, a simpler CI
description: Holds the work the owner's 2026-10-14 decisions (D1-D10 of the cost/code/CI synthesis, quality-gates-internal reports/2026-10-14-cost-code-ci-analysis) moved out of P125 until the segment studies (orchestration, code, CI) produce one consolidated plan. Its tasks are re-planned from those studies before any starts.
desiredOutcome: A task through the plugin costs about 1.25x a plain session above a measured size threshold, the main loop reads one signal line per step, scripts+hooks shrink toward 115k lines with code not above its 3.4.0 count, and CI runs in at most 8 minutes from one executable description of the gate set.

findings.issue: The regenerated ledger directory is still not removed on a signal. ledger_reproducible makes $regen under $TMPDIR and removes it by an explicit rm -rf after ledger_compare returns; an INT or TERM arriving while the generator runs now exits through the new 'exit 130/143' traps, which remove only $WORKDIR, so verify-ledger-* is left behind on that path. The task asks for cleanup 'on every return path', which is met, but the signal path the executor added in the same change leaves the very leak the title names.
findings.resolution: Create the directory under the already-trapped workdir: regen=$(mktemp -d "$WORKDIR/ledger-XXXXXX"). The EXIT trap then covers return, signal and plain exit, and the explicit rm can stay as the early release. Adjust vsh2-vsh4 so their scratch TMPDIR check looks at the workdir.

findings.issue: The vsh5 control passes vacuously when no dash is on PATH: the check is check('vsh5 SKIPPED HERE ...', dash is None), which is True exactly in that branch. It is labelled, but it prints PASS. Likewise vsh2-vsh4 then run under whatever 'sh' is, which may be bash in POSIX mode where a RETURN trap would work, so those cases could not see the defect on that machine.
findings.resolution: Acceptable as labelled for a machine without dash; if the suite has a skip vocabulary, use it so a reader of a clean run sees the control did not run. Otherwise leave as is.

findings.issue: The nt branch of _shim_dir and of the k15 working shim writes .cmd files and is untested on Windows (the executor says so). On the windows CI leg a .cmd found by shutil.which and run without a shell, and a cmd shim that forwards %* to sys.executable, are assumptions; a failure there would turn k13-k15 red on CI only.
findings.resolution: Confirm on the first windows CI run after this lands (ci-every-phase dispatch). If k13-k15 go red there, build the shims as .bat or add the extension to PATHEXT in the case env.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause: the description's fault is 'the report's date inputs render the host placeholder (dd. mm. 2026.) in committed shots', and the task title says committed images 'carry no host format'. The diff pins Intl/Date/navigator.language/number format, but not the native <input type=date> placeholder, which is the one symptom the clause names. I reproduced the limit read-only (in-memory element screenshots, nothing written): on this host (AppleLocale en_US@rg=rszzzz) a bare date input hashes identically under context locale en-US and de-DE with --lang=en-US, and differs only under --lang=de-DE. So the limit is real and the executor's disclosure is accurate. But the disclosure lives only in a code comment: the non-check capture that writes the PNGs prints nothing, and shot()'s pinProblem cannot see the placeholder (it is not in the DOM). A maintainer regenerating shots on such a host commits host-shaped 'filters' / date-input pixels with every check green and a 'pinned' label that now over-claims.
findings.resolution: Make the residual visible at the moment it matters instead of only in a comment. Options, structurally preferred first: (a) in the writing path of shot() (not --check), on darwin read the OS regional format (`defaults read -g AppleLocale`, region suffix `@rg=` other than US) and refuse, or at least print a loud note naming the shots that contain a native date input; (b) add the same reading to machineFingerprint() so --repro and the provenance line quote it. Node's own Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().locale is NOT usable for this: it reports en-US on the overridden host. Alternatively file the date-placeholder half as its own open task/fault so it is tracked rather than documented-away.

findings.issue: The pinned-context assertion runs inside shot(), so a leg that never reaches shot() (e.g. the ladderCtx / prioCtx pages at 7340 and 7415, which drive checks without a shutter) is pinned by option only and unasserted. Today harmless, since they produce no image.
findings.resolution: No action needed unless those contexts ever begin to photograph; if they do, they pass through shot() and are covered. Optionally note this in the PINNED_CONTEXT comment.

findings.issue: The diff changes the answer of _locks.pid_alive for a zombie (True -> False), and the untouched _harness.py states the old one: the comment at 1099-1104 says the product rule 'counts it ALIVE ... the product rule is left as it is', which is now false. _harness._is_zombie and _pid_present (alive is None or not _is_zombie) now duplicate the rule _locks._is_zombie holds, in a second copy that can drift. Both sides of the boundary (product rule, harness restatement of it) are named; the executor disclosed this as NOT DONE because the plan gate refused the file.
findings.resolution: Follow-up task owning _harness.py: reduce _pid_present to `_locks.pid_alive(pid) is not False`, delete the harness _is_zombie, rewrite the comment to say the product rule now reads a zombie as gone. _group_present keeps its own ps walk.

findings.issue: pz3, the over-fire direction of the new retry in acquire, cannot go red: if the `continue` fired on every dead verdict (the mutation pz3 exists to catch), acquire would re-judge the same standing claim forever, because the `continue` skips the `time.monotonic() >= deadline` check and there is no sleep. A regression would hang the suite until the sweep's per-file timeout instead of failing the case. The executor says the same ('would hang rather than fail; not separately mutated'). The 'second direction' case is therefore unproven in the way the repo's no-silent-pass rule asks.
findings.resolution: Bound the retry so a mutation fails by assertion: count retries (a small cap, e.g. re-ask at most a few times, then fall through to the refusal), or make the continue honour the deadline. pz3 then goes red with code != E_STALE instead of hanging. Run the unconditional-continue mutation once to confirm.

findings.issue: The comment above _CHANGE_CLAUSE (and the executor's outcome, 'unknown verbs fall to tdd, the old default') says a verb missing from the list leaves a task at tdd. The code does the opposite: _only_asks_for_test is true when _CHANGE_CLAUSE does NOT match, so an unlisted change verb makes the resolution look test-only and mints regression with no red-first. Probed with the two regexes extracted from the file: 'Add a test for the label, then relocate the prop' -> test-only (regression); 'Add a test for the label and rework the parser' -> test-only; 'Add a test for X; the label should be capitalized' -> test-only; whereas the listed verb 'then fix the prop' -> tdd. A fix task that does require a code change therefore silently loses its red-first discipline whenever its verb is outside the closed list, which is the failure direction the comment promises cannot happen. No test covers an unlisted verb, so the false claim is unguarded.
findings.resolution: fixed in P128.48-izt (92d2ffa87dec): Pick the safe direction on purpose and make the code match: invert the test so regression needs positive evidence, e.g. treat the resolution as test-only only when, after the leading test ask, the rest is a single clause with no further separator-introduced clause (no ', ', '; ', '. ', ' and ', ' then ' continuation beyond the test noun phrase), instead of enumerating change verbs. If the enumeration is kept, correct the comment and outcome to say an unlisted verb yields regression, and add an ALLOW case with an unlisted verb ('then relocate the prop') stating the chosen behaviour.

findings.issue: help_state() is the function that serves the bare GET /api/help and still documents it as 'what every field means, and how the four concepts work'. After this diff its return value (_help.payload()) carries no field text at all; fields are answered by help_field() for ?path=. The diff reworded payload()'s docstring, README, CONTRIBUTING, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE and panel.md for exactly this, but left the docstring of the function across the boundary saying the opposite.
findings.resolution: Reword help_state()'s summary line to say it serves the topics, the guide's card and the lever map, and that a field is answered by help_field() (GET /api/help?path=&doc=).

findings.issue: The deliverable of this task is the writing-path wiring in shot(): the `leak && !ACCEPT_HOST_DATE_FORMAT` refusal, the 'WRITING ... as asked' note, and the `nativeDateInput {regionalFormat, hostFormatAccepted}` entry passed to recordCapture. No test that any gate or vitest run selects reaches it. The nine vitest cases cover only the pure helpers (regionalFormatProblem, regionalFormatBasis, dateInputProblem), and the gate's `shots` command is `--check`, which returns before the refusal. The executor's three mutations were all on those pure functions. Deleting the refusal or the hostFormatAccepted record would leave every recorded gate and the vitest file green. The evidence for the wiring is a manual run (fake osascript, scratch --out) that is not repeatable from the tree.
findings.resolution: Extract the decision in shot() into one pure exported function, e.g. shotDateInputDecision(name, count, facts, accept) returning {refuse, note, extra}, and unit-test it in both directions: leaking host without accept refuses, with accept returns extra.hostFormatAccepted === true, a clean host and a shot with no input return an extra without hostFormatAccepted or no extra. Alternatively add a vitest case that spawns the tool with a fake osascript on PATH.

findings.issue: The escape is recorded (`hostFormatAccepted: true`) but nothing reads the record. screenshot_capture_drift grades version, source digest and hash, and does not look at nativeDateInput. A shot written under --accept-host-date-format therefore passes every committed-artifact check and `--check`, and a reader of the sidecar is the only way to learn it is host-shaped. The record says so honestly, but it is a basis with no claim attached. Capture time is loud (note and warning); the committed state is not.
findings.resolution: File a follow-up task: have screenshot_capture_drift, or the release-set check, report any image whose entry has hostFormatAccepted true, so a release cannot ship host-shaped pictures unnoticed. That is a separate file from this task's scope, so it should be a tracked task rather than an inline edit.

findings.issue: The task is tdd with expectRedFirst true and added exported pure functions, so the test file is owed. It was not declared in `files` or `tests.add`. That is why the helper refused the red-first and the filed return carries testsAdded [] while its outcome claims nine cases in that file. The cases are real and pass on one run: 22 passed in the file. The omission leaves the plan's record of what the task changed incomplete and makes the red-first unprovable by construction.
findings.resolution: Declare tools/ui-tests/capture-provenance.test.mjs in `files` and `tests.add` for this task (with a --introduces red-first, since the symbols are new) before it closes.

tasks.title: fix P128-R7: pz3, the over-fire direction of the new retry in acquire, cannot...
tasks.description:
pz3, the over-fire direction of the new retry in acquire, cannot go red: if the `continue` fired on every dead verdict (the mutation pz3 exists to catch), acquire would re-judge the same standing claim forever, because the `continue` skips the `time.monotonic() >= deadline` check and there is no sleep. A regression would hang the suite until the sweep's per-file timeout instead of failing the case. The executor says the same ('would hang rather than fail; not separately mutated'). The 'second direction' case is therefore unproven in the way the repo's no-silent-pass rule asks.

Resolution asked: Bound the retry so a mutation fails by assertion: count retries (a small cap, e.g. re-ask at most a few times, then fall through to the refusal), or make the continue honour the deadline. pz3 then goes red with code != E_STALE instead of hanging. Run the unconditional-continue mutation once to confirm.
